s1.syndrome_frame: liver mass with possible metastasis in a patient with history of colon cancer
salient_findings: 25 mm lesion in segment 8 of the liver
liver tumor with solid and cystic components
absence of the right portal vein and perfusion defect suggestive of portal vein tumor thrombus
key_facts: 55-year-old man
history of right hemicolectomy for adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon
staged as IIIB (T4N1M0)
no thrombophilic disorders
normal preoperative CEA and CA19-9 levels
completed six months of adjuvant chemotherapy
13 months after surgery, follow-up CT revealed a liver lesion
hepatitis B and C serologies were negative
tumor markers including CEA, CA19-9, α-fetoprotein, and PIVKA-II were within normal limits
liver tumor with two components: solid and cystic
CTAP showed absence of the right portal vein and perfusion defect
endoscopic retrograde cholangiography showed no communication with the biliary tree
bile cytology was negative for malignancy

shortlist.why_kept: liver mass with solid and cystic components, although less likely given normal tumor markers

shortlist.why_kept: liver mass with solid and cystic components, although less likely given patient's history of colon cancer

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon, and the liver lesion was found 13 months after surgery, which is a common timeframe for metastasis to occur. The presence of a solid and cystic component in the liver tumor and the absence of the right portal vein with a perfusion defect are also consistent with metastatic disease.

rejected.label: Hepatocellular carcinoma
rejected.why: Normal tumor markers, including α-fetoprotein, and no evidence of hepatitis B or C infection make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
rejected.why: No communication with the biliary tree and negative bile cytology make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Hepatic adenoma
rejected.why: The presence of a cystic component and the patient's history of colon cancer make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Biliary cystadenocarcinoma
rejected.why: No communication with the biliary tree and the presence of a solid component in the liver tumor make this diagnosis less likely
